Detailed method

One oval sourdough loaf. Currently 500 g flour, 74% hydration, 20% starter, 2% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 370 g water, 100 g starter, and 10 g salt, 980 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 76.4% effective hydration. Currently 1 loaf of 980 g. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 100 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 370 g water, the 100 g starter, and 10 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 74% the dough is soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 3 to 4 hours. Fold it three times in the first 90 minutes. It is ready when it has grown by about half.
  4. Shape Tighten the 980 g into one oval and set it seam-side up in a floured basket. Score one line down the center later. This batch is 1 loaf. The default 980 g uses an oval lidded pot about 30 cm long, or a baking stone with a large roasting pan inverted over it. If you change the amount, use a pot sized to fit.
  5. Proof Cover it for 45 to 75 minutes, until puffy. With 20% starter, bake if the top starts to sink.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with an oval lidded pot inside, or heat a baking stone and a large roasting pan. Place the dough on parchment and lower it, paper and all, into the hot pot. On a stone, set the parchment on the stone and cover it with the roasting pan. Score one line down the center. Bake 20 minutes covered, then 16 to 22 minutes uncovered, until the crust is deep brown. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour.
